```{python}
#| include: false

def embed_example(q: "Quiz", title: str | None = None, height_offset: int = 50) -> None:
    html = q.to_html(title=title).replace('"', '&quot;')
    print(f"""<iframe srcdoc="{html}" onload='javascript:(function(o){{var _height=o.contentWindow.document.body.scrollHeight+{height_offset};o.style.height=_height+"px";}}(this));' style='overflow: hidden;'></iframe>""")
```

See the detailed schema for YAML front matter: [Markdown Input Schema](markdown-schema.qmd)

## Examples by question types

The most typical usecase requires top-level `Q` to define a question and `Quiz` to define a set of questions.

```{python}
from questionsafe import Q, Quiz
```

### True or False Question

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

tfq = (
    Q.TrueFalse(
        name="Logic/DeMorgan",
        questiontext="True or False: Not(A and B) == (Not A) or (Not B)"
    )
    .set_correct_if_true()
)
quiz = Quiz([tfq])  # Pass list of questions to the Quiz constructor
quiz.to_html()      # Or quiz.to_xml() 
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(quiz)
```

### Single Choice Question

From here, I will omit boilerplate code. 

You can set the `questiontext` attribute with more expressive `ask` method. 

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.SingleChoice("SC")
     .ask("Pick one")
     .set_choice_correct("A")      # one correct choice
     .set_choices_wrong("B", "C")  # multiple wrong choices
)
```

Note:
- SingleChoice.add_choice_correct is guarded to prevent adding multiple correct choices via the colorful API. If you need advanced control, use add_answer or set_answers. Validation still requires exactly one correct (fraction=100).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

### Multiple Choice Question

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.MultiChoice(name="MC")
     .ask("Pick all that apply")
     .set_choices_correct("A", "B")  # single/multiple correct choices
     .set_choices_wrong("C", "D")    # multiple wrong choices
     .set_numbering("123")           # abc, ABC, 123, iii, III or none
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```


### Short Answer Question

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.ShortAnswer("SA")
     .ask("Spell 'colour'")
     .add_answer("colour", fraction=100)
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```


### Numerical Question

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Numerical("NU")
     .ask("2+2?")
     .add_answer(4)
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

### Numerical Question (with units)

You can now add answers with units concisely. Global unit options are set once per question.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: true
from questionsafe import Unit

(
    Q.Numerical("Weight")
     .ask("100g + 1kg = ?")
     .add_answer_unit(1100, "g")   # base unit and base answer
     .add_answer_unit(1.1, "kg")   # infer kg multiplier as 1000
     # .set_unit_options(showunits=1, unitgradingtype=2, unitpenalty=0.2)  # optional; defaults are these values
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
embed_example(Quiz([_]))
```

If you prefer to specify units explicitly, `.add_units()` and `.set_units()` accept sensible defaults:

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
from questionsafe import Unit
(
    Q.Numerical("Speed")
     .ask("Give speed in m/s; km/h allowed")
     .add_answer(3.14)
     .add_units(
         Unit("m/s", 1.0, 100),
         Unit("km/h", 0.2777778, 50),
         # All options are optional now; below are the defaults
         showunits=1, unitgradingtype=2, unitpenalty=0.2, unitsleft=False
     )
)
```

### Essay Question

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Essay("E")
     .ask("<p>Introduce yourself.</p>")
)
```

### Description

Description (in Moodle) is a type of question that provides students with some information. 
So, Description type has `name`, `questiontext` and some other metadatas only. 

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Description("Desc/Week1")
     .set_questiontext("<p>This section covers basic topics.</p>")
)
```



### Category

Category (in Moodle) is a meta question that provides the Moodle server with the information about 
how to group the questions that follows. 

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
(
    Q.Category("$course$/Exam/Final")
)
```

## Full Example

This guide covers common tasks: constructing questions, grouping them into a quiz, and rendering.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| results: true
from questionsafe import Q, Quiz, Hint, Text, Unit, Answer
from IPython.display import HTML, display

quiz = Quiz(category="Exam/Week1", subcategory_id="123")
mcq1 = (
    Q.MultiChoice(
        name="Capital/Thailand",
        questiontext="What is the capital of Thailand?"
    )
    .set_choices_correct("Bangkok", feedback="Right!")
    .set_choices_wrong("Chiang Mai", "Phuket", "Pattaya")
    .set_hints(
        Hint("Consider the most populous city.", shownumcorrect=True),
        Hint("Eliminate coastal resort options.", clearwrong=True),
        penalty=0.25
    )
)
quiz.add(mcq1)
quiz.title = "Combined Preview"
embed_example(quiz)
```

### Quickstart: add_answer patterns

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| results: true
from questionsafe import Q, Text
# MultiChoice and SingleChoice
mc = (
    Q.MultiChoice(name="Capitals", questiontext=Text("<p>Pick one</p>"))
    .add_answer("Tokyo", fraction=100)
    .add_answer("Osaka", fraction=0)
)
sc = Q.SingleChoice(name="SC", questiontext=Text("<p>Pick one</p>")).add_answer("A", fraction=100)
mc, sc
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| results: true
# ShortAnswer
from questionsafe import Q, Text
sa = Q.ShortAnswer(name="SA", questiontext=Text("<p>Spell colour</p>")).add_answer("colour", fraction=100)
sa
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| results: true
# Numerical
from questionsafe import Q, Text
nu = Q.Numerical(name="NU", questiontext=Text("<p>2+2?</p>")).add_answer(4)
nu2 = Q.Numerical(name="Pi", questiontext=Text("<p>π (two decimals)?</p>")).add_answer(3.14, tolerance=0.005)
nu, nu2
```

### Advanced: set_answers all at once

When replacing the whole list in one call, construct concrete answers via the Answer interface.

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| results: true
from questionsafe import Answer
from questionsafe import Q, Text
mc = Q.MultiChoice(name="MC", questiontext=Text("<p>Pick two</p>"))
mc.set_answers(
    Answer.Text("A", fraction=50),
    Answer.Text("B", fraction=50),
    Answer.Text("C", fraction=0),
)
mc
```

### Question text formats

MoodleQuiz accepts several convenient forms for questiontext. Strings are treated as HTML by default.

```{python}
#| echo: true
# Minimal (string, default html)
from questionsafe import Q
Q.SingleChoice(name="SC", questiontext="What is the capital of Thailand?")
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
# Explicit Text with default format (html)
from questionsafe import Q, Text
Q.Essay(name="E", questiontext=Text("Introduce yourself."))
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
# Explicit Text with a non-default format (e.g., markdown)
from questionsafe import Q, Text
Q.MultiChoice(
    name="MC-md",
    questiontext=Text("Pick EU capitals:\n\n- Paris\n- Berlin\n- Madrid", format="markdown")
)
```

Note: Moodle often wraps content in paragraph tags automatically; for simple sentences, you can omit surrounding <p>…</p>.

### Recommendation: exporting quizzes

- For typical use (exporting a quiz set), prefer the bound methods on Quiz:
  - quiz.to_xml("out.xml") or quiz.to_html("out.html")
- The top-level functions questionsafe.render_* and questionsafe.write_* are mainly for exporting ad-hoc lists of questions without constructing a Quiz instance (e.g., quick drafts or debugging).

### SingleChoice vs MultiChoice

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q, Text, Answer
# Single-choice: exactly one correct
sc = (
    Q.SingleChoice(name="SC/Capital", questiontext="Capital?")
    .set_choice_correct("Bangkok")
    .set_choices_wrong("Chiang Mai", "Phuket")
)
# Multi-choice: allow multiple correct answers (fractions sum to 100)
mc = Q.MultiChoice(name="MC/EU", questiontext=Text("<p>Pick EU capitals</p>"))
mc.set_answers(
    Answer.from_text("Paris", fraction=50),
    Answer.from_text("Berlin", fraction=50),
    Answer.from_text("Zurich", fraction=0),
)
sc, mc
```

## Project scaffolding and templates

You can scaffold a project and use templates for authoring Markdown questions.

- Initialize a project:

```bash
uv run questionsafe init .
```

This creates the following structure:

```
.
├── questions
├── questionsafe.yml
└── templates
    ├── essay.md.j2
    ├── multichoice.md.j2
    ├── singlechoice.md.j2
    └── ...
```

- Configuration (questionsafe.yml):

```yaml
project:
  questions: ./questions   # authoring root used by `questionsafe create`
  templates: ./templates   # where *.md.j2 templates are discovered
variables:
  ROOT: /absolute/or/relative/path  # available as $ROOT (overrides OS env)
```

Variable expansion (Reader)
- The Markdown Reader expands ~, $VAR and ${VAR} using variables from questionsafe.yml in the current working directory; if a variable is not defined there, it falls back to the OS environment.
- Applied to:
  - include: "$ROOT/inc.yml"
  - cloze:
    gap1:
      file: "$ROOT/schoice.md"
  - essay:
    response.textarea.template:
      path: "$ROOT/template.md"
    graderinfo:
      path: "$ROOT/grading-guide.md"
- CLI templates also receive a VARS mapping so you can reference {{ VARS.ROOT }} in templates if needed.

- Creating new questions from templates:

```bash
uv run questionsafe create   # interactive prompts
uv run questionsafe create questions/q1.md --name "Sample/SC" --type singlechoice
```

- Templates:
  - Discovered by listing `*.md.j2` files in the configured templates directory.
  - The filename stem is the template name (e.g., numerical_unit.md.j2 -> `--type numerical_unit`).
  - Jinja2 context provides `name` for use in front matter.

## Cloze (embedded)

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe import Q, Reader
# Build sub-questions
sc = Reader("schoice.md").read().set_name("gap1")
mc = Reader("mchoice.md").read().set_name("gap2")
# Embed into a Cloze stem
clz = (
  Q.Cloze("Japan/Cities")
  .ask("The capital of Japan is {{gap1}}.\nChoose stations in Tokyo.\n{{gap2}}")
  .embed_question(sc)
  .embed_question(mc, orientation="h", weight=2)
)
clz
```

### Categories

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe.quiz import Quiz
from questionsafe import Q
quiz = Quiz(category="Course/Week1")
# Inherits parent category: rendered as $course$/Course/Week1/Intro
quiz.add_category("Intro")
# Absolute category path (no inheritance): rendered as $course$/Intro-Absolute
quiz.add_category("Intro-Absolute", inherit=False)
quiz
```

Note: the writer normalizes category paths by prefixing the first segment with $course$/ unless the first segment is an explicit token like $course$ (i.e., matches ^\$.+\$$).

### Grouping with QuestionGroup

You can explicitly group variants using QuestionGroup. This is equivalent to passing a list, but allows attaching metadata and reusing groups.

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe.base import QuestionGroup
from questionsafe import Q, Text
from questionsafe.quiz import Quiz
# Build two variants of the same logical question
v1 = Q.TrueFalse(name="Logic/DM/1", questiontext=Text("...")).set_correct_if_true()
v2 = Q.TrueFalse(name="Logic/DM/2", questiontext=Text("...")).set_correct_if_true()
# Wrap them in a group and add to the quiz
quiz = Quiz(category="Course/Week1")
quiz.add_group(QuestionGroup([v1, v2]), idnumber_prefix="dm-", idnumber_offset=0)
quiz
```
